climate.overview_html: The Copernicus Climate Change Service confirmed on September 10 that August 2026 tied July 2023 as the joint hottest month in the 177-year ERA5 record — global average surface air temperature 16.96°C, or 1.65°C above the 1850–1900 pre-industrial average — with extra-polar sea surface temperatures also breaking the August record at 21.07°C. A new mooring-based study from the University of Miami published September 22 provides some of the clearest direct observational evidence yet that the AMOC has been losing strength for nearly two decades, with the weakening signal now confirmed at four separate latitudes across the western North Atlantic boundary from 16.5°N to 42.5°N. At the UNGA Climate Summit convened September 23, Secretary-General Gu­terres assembled heads of government, business and finance for renewed pledges on accelerated clean energy deployment and doubled climate finance, with urgency amplified by the Super El Niño-driven loss record already spanning Bangkok’s worst flooding since 2011, the costliest Japanese typhoon season on record, and Western Europe’s hottest summer since 2003.

items.headline: Copernicus C3S: August 2026 Ties July 2023 as Joint Hottest Month on Record; Global Average 16.96°C; 1.65°C Above Pre-Industrial; Extra-Polar SSTs Break August Record at 21.07°C; Western Europe Surpasses 2003 Summer Heat Record; Super El Niño + GHG Forcing Combined Driver
items.summary: The Copernicus Climate Change Service September 10 monthly bulletin confirms that August 2026 equalled July 2023 as the joint hottest month in the ERA5 record. Global average surface air temperature reached 16.96°C, 0.85°C above the 1991–2020 ERA5 reference average and 1.65°C above the estimated 1850–1900 pre-industrial baseline — pushing global temperatures back above 1.5°C for the fourth consecutive month. Extra-polar ocean surface temperatures also set an August record at 21.07°C, surpassing the record set in August 2023. In Western Europe, the summer of 2026 broke the extreme set in the 2003 European heat wave, with prolonged heatwaves beginning as early as May driven by anomalous subtropical ridge extensions. Copernicus attributes the record to the combined effect of greenhouse gas-induced long-term warming trend and the continuing Super El Niño in the equatorial Pacific, which amplifies global mean SSTs with a 3–6 month lag. The August outcome adds to growing confidence that 2026 will rank as the second-warmest calendar year in the instrumental record, consistent with Carbon Brief’s central estimate of approximately 1.51°C for the full year.

items.source: University of Miami Rosenstiel School / ScienceDaily
items.headline: University of Miami: Clearest Direct Observational Evidence Yet of 2-Decade AMOC Weakening; Four Western-Boundary Mooring Stations from 16.5°N to 42.5°N Show Coherent Decline Since 2004; Consistent With Modelling Projections of 50%+ Weakening by 2100
items.summary: Researchers at the University of Miami Rosenstiel School used temperature, salinity and velocity data from four mooring stations along the western boundary of the North Atlantic — measuring continuously since 2004 — to document a coherent weakening of the AMOC across the basin for nearly two decades. The signal was confirmed consistently at four latitudes from 16.5°N to 42.5°N, distinguishing this result from regional current anomalies and providing among the most direct observational evidence so far of basin-wide AMOC decline. The finding complements both the RAPID-MOCHA array data at 26°N and proxy-reconstruction studies, and is quantitatively consistent with the April 2026 Science Advances study by Portmann et al. that projected a 51 ± 8% weakening by 2100 under SSP2-4.5 using observational constraints. A continued AMOC decline would alter precipitation patterns across Europe and eastern North America, accelerate sea-level rise on the US East Coast, and reduce the northward ocean heat transport that moderates Northern Hemisphere climate.

items.headline: UNGA Climate Summit September 23, 2026: Guterres Convenes Leaders on Faster Clean Energy, Doubled Climate Finance and Resilience; Super El Niño Extremes Amplify Urgency; Limiting Overshoot Framework Centred
items.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres convened a Climate Summit on the sidelines of UNGA 81 on September 23, 2026, focused on accelerating implementation rather than new pledges. Participants from more than 80 governments, corporations and financial institutions committed to faster deployment of proven clean energy technologies, doubling of climate finance flows to developing nations by 2030, and strengthened national resilience and adaptation plans. The summit came against the backdrop of the ongoing Super El Niño — the strongest in the modern instrumental record — which has amplified weather extremes globally in 2026. Guterres used the gathering to emphasise the UN Limiting Overshoot framework, arguing that rapid decarbonisation can limit the duration and peak of any 1.5°C overshoot even if the target is briefly exceeded.

major_events.name: Tropical Storm Queenie (Surigae / JTWC 25W) — WEAKENED; APPROACHING HONSHU; ASIAN GAMES 2026 AT RISK
major_events.status: TROPICAL STORM — weakened significantly to ~85 km/h sustained winds as of September 30; located approximately 750 km SSW of Yokosuka, Japan, tracking ENE at 22 km/h; forecast to approach Izu Islands and Aichi/Tōkai coast around Thursday–Friday October 1–2 before extratropical transition October 3; previously peaked at 240 km/h maximum sustained winds
major_events.impact: Asian Games 2026 Aichi-Nagoya entering final week; ~4,000 athletes housed on cruise ship Costa Serena at elevated risk; outdoor competition days under review; Aichi region already received 104 mm/hr record rainfall September 22 from Typhoon Dujuan (which killed 162 people and caused $22 B in damages); compound storm fatigue and soil saturation elevate flood and landslide risk with even a weakened Queenie approach

major_events.name: Hurricane Polo Remnants (Eastern Pacific) — FLOODING U.S. SOUTHWEST
major_events.status: POST-TROPICAL REMNANTS — Polo made landfall in Baja California Sur at 110 mph (Cat 2-equivalent) on September 30 morning before weakening rapidly inland; post-tropical moisture sweeping northeast into US Southwest by afternoon September 30; East Fork Virgin River near Zion National Park in raging flood; dam failure threat on Rio Grande in south-central New Mexico
major_events.impact: Emergency evacuations ordered in Rincon, Salem and Garfield, New Mexico over Rio Grande dam failure risk; desert highways and arroyos flooded across southern Utah, Arizona and New Mexico; heavy rain extending into Texas and Oklahoma overnight September 30; pre-wetted soils from earlier September monsoon amplifying runoff response

major_events.name: 2026 Bangkok / Thailand Floods — DRAINING; RECOVERY UNDERWAY
major_events.status: RECOVERING — all 50 Bangkok districts declared flood disaster zones September 26; peak flooding September 24–28; 300–330 mm rain fell in 48 hours in hardest-hit areas; Bangkok Metropolitan Administration reported 2–3 days remaining for full drainage as of September 29; Thai Cabinet declared September 28–29 emergency public holidays in Bangkok and three surrounding provinces
major_events.impact: 8 deaths; 52,000+ households inundated; 4,900+ people evacuated to shelters; heavy traffic disruption at 37 locations across the city; flooding driven by tropical depression combined with an anomalously active monsoon trough; one of Bangkok’s worst flood events since 2011

major_events.name: 2026 Southeast Asian Haze
major_events.status: ACTIVE — Singapore PSI in moderate-to-unhealthy range; >617,400 fire hotspots in Indonesia as of September 14; ASEAN Level 3 alert ongoing since August 1; 895,000+ ha burned as of late August
major_events.impact: Health advisories across Singapore, Malaysia, Brunei, Philippines, Vietnam; >12 million people affected; >1.4 million students in remote learning; smoke forecast through October or early November as Super El Niño delays Indonesian wet-season onset; hotspot count nearly double the same period in 2019

major_events.name: 2026 Europe Wildfire Season
major_events.status: ACTIVE — 678,978 ha burned as of September 23 (91% above 20-year average); very extreme fire danger forecast southern France, northern Spain and Portugal through September 30; France has burned close to 100,000 ha (record over 20 years of satellite measurement)
major_events.impact: Air quality warnings across Iberian Peninsula and southern France; EU uninsured losses estimated €40–60 billion; EU Climate Insurance Alliance announced September 16 in response; active fire danger also persisting in Italy, Balkans and the Caucasus

major_events.status: WINDING DOWN — 1,873 fires burned 2,543,011 acres as of September 22; most major fires at 97–100% containment; BIG GRASS Fire (578,637 acres, Malheur County) at 94% containment; elevated fire-weather continues in Northern California
major_events.impact: 2 deaths; season exceeded 2020 Oregon record and ranks among worst ever; NIFC maintains above-normal fire potential through October in Northern California under Super El Niño precipitation deficits; humidity 10–25%, gusts to 40 mph Sierra Nevada through week

weather.overview_html: Two new high-impact systems define September 30. Former Hurricane Polo’s post-tropical remnants swept across the U.S. Southwest on September 30, flooding desert highways and triggering emergency evacuations in three New Mexico communities over dam-failure concerns along the Rio Grande; the heavy rain threat extends into Texas and Oklahoma overnight. In Thailand, all 50 Bangkok districts were declared flood disaster zones after 300–330 mm fell in 48 hours, inundating 52,000 households and killing eight — the city’s worst flooding since 2011; drainage is now expected within 24 hours. Meanwhile, what was Typhoon Queenie (Surigae) has weakened sharply to ~85 km/h as it approaches the Aichi-Nagoya corridor — threatening the closing days of the 2026 Asian Games and raising concern for the ~4,000 athletes housed on the Costa Serena cruise ship. Hurricane Nolo in the Central Pacific has weakened from Category 4 to Category 3 (115 mph / 958 hPa) after dropping more than 12 inches of rain on Maui and the Big Island without making landfall, and is now forecast to turn away from the main Hawaiian Islands.

items.headline: Tropical Storm Queenie (Surigae) UPDATED September 30: Weakened to ~85 km/h from 240 km/h Peak; 750 km SSW Yokosuka; Approaching Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games Venues October 1–2; ~4,000 Athletes on Costa Serena Cruise Ship at Risk; Extratropical Transition October 3; Compound Risk After Typhoon Dujuan ($22B Damage, 162 Deaths)
items.summary: Typhoon Queenie (Surigae, JTWC 25W, JMA Typhoon No. 26) has weakened substantially as it moves northeast south of Honshu, dropping from its 240 km/h peak intensity earlier in the week to approximately 85 km/h sustained winds as of September 30 — below the typhoon threshold of 120 km/h. The centre is located approximately 750 km south-southwest of Yokosuka, tracking east-northeastward at 22 km/h. The forecast track brings the weakened storm toward the Izu Islands and the Aichi-Tōkai-Kantō coastal region around Thursday–Friday, October 1–2, by which time it is expected to produce heavy rain and gusty winds in Aichi Prefecture. The approach threatens outdoor events in the final days of the 2026 Asian Games Aichi-Nagoya, with particular concern for the approximately 4,000 athletes and officials housed on the Costa Serena cruise ship in Nagoya harbour. Organisers have flagged that indoor venues are unaffected but outdoor events including athletics and road cycling face schedule uncertainty. The storm arrives just eight days after Typhoon Dujuan — the costliest typhoon in Japanese history at $22.19 billion in damage and 162 deaths, mostly in Hokkaido — leaving soils near saturation and communities still in recovery.

items.source: CNN / Bangkok Post / US Embassy Bangkok
items.headline: Bangkok 2026 Floods: All 50 Districts Declared Disaster Zones September 26; 300–330 mm Rain in 48 Hours; 8 Deaths; 52,000 Households Inundated; 4,900 Evacuated; Thai Cabinet Declares Emergency Holidays; Worst Flooding Since 2011
items.summary: A catastrophic rainfall event struck Bangkok between September 24 and 28, 2026, driven by a persistent low-pressure system embedded in an anomalously active southwest monsoon trough. Rainfall totals reached 300–330 mm over 48 hours in the worst-affected areas, with canals overflowing and drainage systems overwhelmed. The Bangkok Metropolitan Administration declared all 50 districts flood disaster zones on September 26. Eight people died; approximately 52,000 households were inundated and 4,900 residents evacuated to emergency shelters. Main road traffic was disrupted at 37 locations across the city. The Thai Cabinet declared September 28 and 29 as emergency public holidays in Bangkok, Pathum Thani, Samut Prakan and Nonthaburi. The BMA estimated 2–3 days for full drainage after the rain stopped. The event is the city’s worst flooding since the 2011 mega-flood, which inundated approximately one third of Thailand’s territory. Climate attribution analyses note that Super El Niño conditions in 2026 have significantly intensified the Southeast Asian monsoon season, elevating precipitation extremes across the region.

items.headline: Hurricane Polo Remnants SEPTEMBER 30: Baja California Sur Landfall at 110 mph September 30 Morning; Post-Tropical Moisture Flooding U.S. Southwest; New Mexico Dam Failure Threat Evacuates Rincon, Salem and Garfield; Heavy Rain Extending to Texas and Oklahoma Overnight
items.summary: Hurricane Polo made landfall in the Mexican state of Baja California Sur on the morning of September 30 with maximum sustained winds of 110 mph before weakening rapidly as it moved inland to the northeast. The storm’s post-tropical remnants swept moisture into the U.S. Southwest by Tuesday afternoon. Desert rivers and normally dry arroyos surged with floodwater across southern Utah, Arizona and New Mexico. The East Fork of the Virgin River near Zion National Park crested dramatically, with debris including at least one shipping container floating downstream. In south-central New Mexico, the potential failure of a dam prompted mandatory evacuations of the communities of Rincon, Salem and Garfield, whose combined population of several hundred residents was ordered to seek higher ground along the Rio Grande. The heavy rain threat was forecast to spread into Texas and Oklahoma beginning Tuesday night, with flash-flood watches issued across a broad swath of the Southern Plains. The Polo event follows an anomalously active September in the Eastern and Central Pacific under the Super El Niño pattern, which has suppressed Atlantic hurricane activity while generating multiple major Pacific storms.

renewables.overview_html: Eurostat data published September 18 confirms that renewables supplied 54.1% of EU electricity generation in Q2 2026, with solar now the single largest renewable source at 41.6% of the renewable mix — up sharply from 37.0% a year earlier. Two significant portfolio transactions closed this week: Apex Clean Energy and Thailand-based EGCO Group completed a 49% stake sale in a 339 MW operational US solar and wind portfolio (the 150 MW Coldwater solar project in Michigan and the 189 MW Timbermill wind project in North Carolina) on September 25 under long-term PPAs; and India’s KPI Green Energy entered a binding offer on September 30 to acquire 100% of Alfanar Energy and Netra Wind, adding 507.9 MW of operational wind capacity in Gujarat’s Kutch region for ₹2,410 crore, continuing the rapid consolidation of Indian wind assets ahead of grid expansion. A Solar Quarter analysis published September 29 projects Europe’s power sector will surpass 80% zero-carbon generation by 2030, though the EU27 is forecast to reach only 63.7% renewable share — below both the 65% Fit-for-55 and 69% REPowerEU targets.

items.headline: Eurostat: 54.1% of EU Electricity from Renewables in Q2 2026; Solar Now 41.6% of Renewable Mix (Up from 37.0% Q2 2025); Latvia 97.7%, Denmark 94.3% Country Leaders; Wind Second at 27.7%; Hydro Third at 22.6%
items.summary: Eurostat's September 18 quarterly release confirms that renewable energy sources supplied 54.1% of total EU electricity generation in the second quarter of 2026, a slight decrease from 54.3% in Q2 2025 but sustained at more than half for a second consecutive year. Solar PV has emerged as the single largest component of EU renewable electricity at 41.6% of the renewable total, up from 37.0% in Q2 2025, reflecting continued record capacity additions. Wind power is the second-largest source at 27.7%, followed by hydropower at 22.6%. Member state performance ranges from Latvia (97.7%, dominated by hydro and solar), Denmark (94.3%, dominated by wind) and Croatia (92.2%, dominated by hydro) at the top, to Slovakia (19.8%), Czechia (20.9%) and Malta (24.5%) at the bottom. The aggregate figure highlights that the EU has reached structural majority renewable electricity generation but faces distributional challenges in member states heavily dependent on fossil generation.

items.source: PV Tech / Apex Clean Energy / EGCO Group
items.headline: Apex Clean Energy and EGCO Group Close 49% Stake Sale in 339 MW US Solar and Wind Portfolio: 150 MW Coldwater Solar (Michigan) + 189 MW Timbermill Wind (North Carolina); Second Capital Recycling Deal Between the Two Parties; Both Projects Under Long-Term PPAs
items.summary: Apex Clean Energy and Thailand-based Electricity Generating Public Company Limited (EGCO Group) completed the acquisition by EGCO of a 49% membership interest in two operational US renewable energy projects on September 25, 2026. The portfolio comprises the 150 MW Coldwater solar project in Michigan and the 189 MW Timbermill wind project in North Carolina. Both projects are contracted under long-term power purchase agreements. Apex retains the 51% majority interest and continues as project operator. This is the second capital recycling deal the two companies have executed, following an October 2025 transaction covering an earlier 251 MW solar and wind portfolio. The structure demonstrates EGCO’s strategy of acquiring operating minority stakes in contracted US renewable assets as a capital-efficient route to growing its international clean-energy exposure. Financial terms were not disclosed.

items.headline: KPI Green Energy Enters Binding Offer to Acquire Alfanar Energy and Netra Wind for ₹2,410 Crore: 507.9 MW Operational Wind Capacity in Gujarat Kutch Region; Transaction Expected Close by 28 February 2027; Largest Single Indian Wind Asset Acquisition of 2026
items.summary: KPI Green Energy announced on September 30, 2026 that it has entered a binding offer to acquire 100% of Alfanar Energy and Netra Wind, adding 507.9 MW of operational wind power capacity located in the Kutch region of Gujarat. The acquisition consideration of ₹2,410 crore (approximately $290 million) reflects a premium to recent Indian wind asset transaction multiples, driven by the Kutch region’s high-capacity-factor wind resource and proximity to major industrial load centres. The transaction is expected to close by February 28, 2027, subject to regulatory approvals. KPI Green, which has been among the fastest-growing renewable developers in India, describes the acquisition as accelerating its strategy of combining utility-scale wind with captive and open-access power supply to commercial and industrial customers. India’s installed solar capacity crossed 160 GW in 2026, and the wind sector is entering a period of rapid consolidation as established projects trade at premiums reflecting the difficulty of securing new grid connections.

items.headline: Europe Power Sector on Track to Surpass 80% Zero-Carbon Generation by 2030; But EU27 Renewables Forecast at 63.7% by 2030 — Below 65% Fit-for-55 and 69% REPowerEU Targets; Solar and Storage Leading Growth; Grid Investment the Binding Constraint
items.summary: A September 29 analysis projects that Europe’s combined power sector across 35 markets will surpass 80% zero-carbon generation (renewables plus nuclear) by 2030, driven by continued solar and battery storage additions. However, within the EU27 specifically, renewables alone are forecast to supply approximately 63.7% of electricity by 2030 — short of the 65% Fit-for-55 target and well below the 69% REPowerEU goal. The gap is attributed primarily to slower-than-planned offshore wind development in the North Sea and Baltic regions due to supply chain constraints and grid connection delays, and to continued fossil gas dependence in several Central and Eastern European member states. Solar PV and utility-scale battery storage are the two fastest-growing components. Grid infrastructure investment is identified as the binding constraint for further renewable integration, with the European Commission’s Grid Action Plan of January 2026 yet to translate into significantly accelerated permitting timelines.

science.overview_html: WeatherNext 3 (arXiv:2609.03582, September 3, 2026) from Google Research introduces hourly probabilistic global forecasts at 0.1° resolution by training directly on low-latency geostationary satellite observations, outperforming both its predecessor WeatherNext 2 and ECMWF’s AIFS ENS v2 and setting a new state of the art for ML weather prediction. A complementary model, TC-Next (arXiv:2609.02085, September 2) applies zero-shot multimodal deep learning to tropical cyclone track and intensity forecasting at 6–24 h lead times — directly relevant to operational cyclone guidance under the active Super El Niño Pacific season. At the university research level, Schmitt et al. (arXiv:2609.03210, submitted to Science) show that injecting real observational data directly into an AI weather model at inference time improves precipitation forecasts significantly — a key result for bridging the gap between reanalysis-trained models and real-time operational skill. In direct air capture, Climeworks reported on September 10 that its Mammoth plant in Iceland achieved a fivefold increase in net CO2 removal output in H1 2026 (675 tonnes vs. 119 tonnes in H1 2025), while operating costs fell more than 50% — the most significant performance leap reported by any operational DAC facility to date.

items.headline: WeatherNext 3 (arXiv:2609.03582): Hourly Probabilistic Global Forecasts at 0.1° Resolution Trained Directly on Geostationary Satellite Observations; Outperforms WeatherNext 2 and ECMWF AIFS ENS v2; New State of the Art for ML Weather Prediction; Includes Solar Radiation and Cloud Cover
items.summary: WeatherNext 3 extends the WeatherNext framework to generate new probabilistic global weather forecasts every hour by ingesting low-latency geostationary satellite data directly, bypassing dependence on numerical analysis cycles. The model operates at 0.1° spatial resolution with hourly time steps and includes single-level variables rarely covered by earlier ML models, including solar radiation and cloud cover. In systematic evaluation, WeatherNext 3 sets a new state of the art for probabilistic weather prediction, outperforming both the prior WeatherNext 2 system and ECMWF’s AIFS ENS v2, currently the leading operational ensemble from a major meteorological centre. The hourly temporal resolution and satellite-direct training make the system particularly relevant to nowcasting-to-short-range applications and to users in regions where conventional radiosonde and surface observation networks are sparse. The result is directly relevant to renewable energy forecasting, where intra-hour solar irradiance and wind variability drive dispatch and balancing decisions.

items.headline: TC-Next (arXiv:2609.02085): Zero-Shot Multimodal Deep Learning for Tropical Cyclone Track and Intensity Forecasting at 6–24 h; Directly Relevant to Super El Niño Season Active Cyclone Guidance
items.summary: TC-Next introduces a zero-shot multimodal deep learning framework for tropical cyclone forecasting that predicts both track and intensity at 6–2 lead times without requiring storm-specific fine-tuning. The zero-shot capability — the model generalises to cyclone cases not seen during training — is enabled by multimodal fusion of satellite imagery, reanalysis fields and storm metadata. The approach is designed to improve guidance in real time even for unusual or rapidly intensifying storms for which historical analogues are scarce. The 2026 Pacific season under the Super El Niño has produced an unusually high number of rapidly intensifying systems, including the active season in the Western Pacific that led to Typhoons Dujuan and Queenie in September, making rapid-intensification skill particularly operationally relevant.

items.headline: Schmitt et al. (arXiv:2609.03210, Submitted to Science): Injecting Real Observations Into AI Weather Model at Inference Improves Precipitation Forecasts; Bridges Gap Between Reanalysis-Trained ML Models and Real-Time Operational Skill
items.meta: Julian F. Schmitt, Bertrand Delorme, Robert C. King et al. · arXiv:2609.03210 [physics.ao-ph] · Submitted to Science · Submitted 2 September 2026, revised 10 September 2026
items.summary: Schmitt, Delorme, King and colleagues address one of the key operational gaps in AI weather forecasting: the discrepancy between skill evaluated on reanalysis and skill delivered in real time, where actual observations differ from the idealised reanalysis inputs on which models are trained. The paper demonstrates that directly injecting observational data into an AI weather model at inference time — rather than relying solely on analysis-derived initial conditions — yields significant improvements in precipitation forecasts. The result is submitted to Science, indicating the authors and reviewers regard it as a finding of broad scientific significance. The methodology is directly applicable to operational systems that must ingest incomplete, irregular and noisy real-time observations and offers a route to closing the reanalysis-to-operation skill gap that currently limits the practical value of data-driven weather models.

items.source: University of Miami Rosenstiel School / ScienceDaily
items.headline: New AMOC Study: Four Western North Atlantic Mooring Stations Confirm Coherent 2-Decade Weakening from 16.5°N to 42.5°N; Clearest Direct Observational Evidence Yet; Consistent With Portmann et al. 50%+ Projection; Implications for European Climate, US East Coast Sea Level
items.meta: University of Miami Rosenstiel School of Marine, Atmospheric, and Earth Science · ScienceDaily press release · 22 September 2026
items.summary: Using temperature, salinity and velocity data from four direct-measurement mooring stations along the western boundary of the North Atlantic (continuously recording since 2004) at latitudes spanning 16.5°N to 42.5°N, University of Miami researchers document a coherent long-term weakening of the AMOC across the full width of the basin over nearly two decades. The consistency of the decline signal at four independent latitudes distinguishes this result from regional current anomalies and provides among the strongest direct observational evidence to date of basin-wide AMOC deceleration. The April 2026 Science Advances study by Portmann et al. (doi:10.1126/sciadv.adx4298) used observational constraints to project a 51 ± 8% AMOC weakening by 2100 under SSP2-4.5, roughly 60% more than climate models alone suggest. A further weakening of the AMOC would alter European precipitation, accelerate US East Coast sea-level rise, and reduce the ocean heat transport that moderates Northern Hemisphere climate — consequences relevant to both climate-risk assessment and physical climate modelling for atmospheric scientists and ML practitioners working on climate projection.

items.headline: Climeworks Mammoth DAC Plant: Fivefold Net CO<sub>2</sub> Removal Increase in H1 2026 (675 Tonnes vs. 119 Tonnes H1 2025); Operating Costs More Than Halved; Upgraded Sorbent Formulation and Mechanical Redesign Key Drivers; Full Module Upgrade Planned End-2026
items.summary: Climeworks reported on September 10 that net carbon dioxide removal output at its Mammoth direct air capture plant in Iceland increased more than fivefold in the first half of 2026: 675 tonnes of net CDR in H1 2026 versus 119 tonnes in H1 2025. Operating costs fell by more than 50% over the same period. The performance gains are attributed to two categories of improvement: refinements to the sorbent (filter material) formulation and production process to increase CO2 capture capacity, and mechanical redesign and equipment upgrades to the collector containers and operating processes that improve throughput and reduce energy consumption per tonne. Climeworks states that upgraded collector containers have more than doubled CO2 capture performance under real-world operating conditions. The company plans to roll out the new sorbent and mechanical upgrades across all 12 collector containers in a full plant module by end-2026. Mammoth, the world’s largest operational direct air capture plant at the time of its 2024 commissioning, has been widely criticised for underperforming against initial capacity projections; the H1 2026 performance data represent the most significant turnaround reported by any operational DAC facility and are closely watched as a signal of whether gigaton-scale DAC is achievable within the timeframe of current climate commitments.

items.title: KPI Green Energy Acquires Alfanar Energy and Netra Wind: 507.9 MW India Wind at ₹2,410 Crore; Gujarat Kutch Region; Close Expected February 2027; Largest Single Indian Wind Asset Acquisition of 2026
items.body_html: KPI Green Energy entered a binding offer on September 30 to acquire 100% of Alfanar Energy and Netra Wind for ₹2,410 crore (≈$290 million), adding 507.9 MW of operational wind power capacity in Gujarat’s Kutch region — described by analysts as the largest single wind asset acquisition in India in 2026. The Kutch site is one of India’s highest-capacity-factor onshore wind corridors, and acquiring operational assets avoids multi-year grid interconnection queues that constrain greenfield development. KPI Green positions the acquisition as accelerating its strategy of combining utility-scale generation with captive and open-access C&I power supply contracts. The transaction is expected to close by 28 February 2027 subject to regulatory approval. KPI Green shares rose 4% on news of the deal. Indian wind consolidation is accelerating in 2026 as installed solar crosses 160 GW and utilities seek contracted clean-power supply chains to serve hyperscale data-centre and manufacturing demand.

items.title: Apex Clean Energy and EGCO Group Close 339 MW US Solar and Wind Stake Sale: 150 MW Coldwater Solar (Michigan) + 189 MW Timbermill Wind (North Carolina); 49% to EGCO; Second Capital Recycling Deal for the Pair in Twelve Months
items.body_html: Apex Clean Energy and Thailand’s EGCO Group completed on September 25 a 49% stake sale in a 339 MW portfolio of operational US renewable projects — the 150 MW Coldwater solar project in Michigan and the 189 MW Timbermill wind project in North Carolina — both contracted under long-term power purchase agreements. EGCO’s press release describes the portfolio as “Pinnacle IV” and frames the acquisition as part of its overseas renewable growth strategy, contributing contracted generation to its earnings from the date of close. Apex retains a 51% majority interest and continues as operator. This is the second capital recycling deal the two parties have executed in twelve months, following an October 2025 transaction covering 251 MW of earlier-generation solar and wind assets. The repeat transaction illustrates a growing pattern of US independent power producers recycling operating asset equity to Asian strategic investors with long-dated clean energy targets.
items.source_html: PV Tech / EGCO Group

items.title: Climeworks Mammoth DAC Fivefold Output Increase and 50%+ Cost Cut in H1 2026: Most Significant Operational DAC Performance Turnaround Reported to Date; Full Module Upgrade Planned End-2026
items.body_html: Climeworks announced on September 10 that net CO2 removal output at its Mammoth direct air capture plant in Iceland reached 675 tonnes in H1 2026 — a fivefold increase from 119 tonnes in H1 2025 — while operating costs fell by more than 50%, the most significant operational turnaround reported by any DAC facility to date. Climeworks attributes the gains to an upgraded sorbent formulation that increases CO2 capture capacity, combined with mechanical redesign of collector containers and refined operating processes that reduce energy use per tonne captured. The company plans to roll out the improved sorbent and mechanical package across all 12 collector containers in a complete plant module by end-2026, which would substantially raise total facility output. ESG Today notes that Mammoth had been widely criticised for underperforming its initial capacity projections since commissioning in 2024, making the H1 2026 data particularly significant as evidence that the technology can improve substantially at industrial scale. The result is closely watched by the carbon removal industry as a signal of whether engineered DAC can reach cost and capacity milestones that would allow meaningful contribution to net-zero pathways by 2035–2040.
items.source_html: Carbon Pulse / Climeworks / ESG Today
